memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate." — Gen 3:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God now turns to the woman with the same patient searching: "What is this you have done?" Again there is room for honest confession. And again, the answer comes wrapped in blame — "The serpent deceived me."

To be fair, there was truth in her words. She had been deceived; the serpent really did lie to her (1 Tim 2:14). But notice how the pattern repeats. Adam blamed Eve, Eve blames the serpent, and no one is willing simply to stand still and own their part. Each one is true about someone else's fault while quietly sidestepping their own. It is easier to explain how we were led into sin than to admit that we chose it.

Yet look closely, and there is a small mercy even here. Eve does end with two honest words: "and I ate." Buried beneath the excuse is a flicker of truth. Sometimes our confessions are like that — mixed, imperfect, still reaching for reasons — and yet God, in His kindness, hears the honest part.

Dear friend, we may be genuinely sinned against, genuinely deceived, genuinely wounded by others — and still be responsible for how we respond. The Gospel does not ask us to pretend we were never wronged. It simply invites us to bring our own "and I ate" honestly to God, trusting that Christ has borne the weight of it, and that grace meets the heart brave enough to confess.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you find it easier to talk about how you were wronged than to own your own choices?
2. Even when you have truly been deceived or hurt, what part is yours to confess?
3. How does knowing Christ has borne your sin make honest confession safer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You gently seek the truth from me rather than leaving me to hide. Even when I have been deceived or wronged, help me to own my part honestly before You. Thank You that Jesus bore my sin, so I can confess without fear. Amen.
